0:00-0:03:
Continue directly from the previous scene.

The filtered customer rows slide in from the LEFT side of the frame and transform into a floating table positioned on the LEFT side of <Subject 1>.

The table is labelled exactly:

CUSTOMERS

It contains exactly THREE columns:

customer_id
name
city

It contains exactly FOUR rows:

101 | Anna | Melbourne
102 | Carlo | Melbourne
103 | Faye | Melbourne
104 | Hannah | Melbourne

At the same time, a second floating table slides in from the RIGHT side of the frame.

The second table is labelled exactly:

ORDERS

It contains exactly FOUR columns:

order_id
customer_id
product
total

It contains exactly FIVE rows:

5001 | 101 | Laptop | $1800
5002 | 103 | Mouse | $45
5003 | 101 | Monitor | $420
5004 | 104 | Keyboard | $120
5005 | 999 | Headphones | $200

<Subject 1> stands exactly between the two tables.

He points his LEFT hand toward the CUSTOMERS table and his RIGHT hand toward the ORDERS table.

<Subject 1> says:
<d>[English, Neutral Filipino Male Voice] Anna’s details are in one table, while her purchases are stored in another.</d>

0:03-0:06:
Fast punch-in to the space between both tables.

The value:

101

in Anna’s customer_id cell on the CUSTOMERS table becomes surrounded by a thick glowing yellow circle.

At the same time, both occurrences of:

101

in the ORDERS table become surrounded by identical glowing yellow circles.

These are specifically:

5001 | 101 | Laptop | $1800
5003 | 101 | Monitor | $420

Exactly TWO thick hand-drawn yellow connecting lines animate from Anna’s customer_id value 101 on the LEFT table to the two matching customer_id values 101 on the RIGHT table.

The first connection lands on order 5001 with a sharp CLICK.

The second connection lands on order 5003 with another sharp CLICK.

No lines connect to customer_id 103, 104, or 999 during this example.

<Subject 1> points directly at the matching number 101.

<Subject 1> says:
<d>[English, Neutral Filipino Male Voice] JOIN works because customer ID one-oh-one appears in both tables.</d>

The two matching order rows detach from the ORDERS table and slide toward Anna’s row.

The following three pieces of information visibly combine:

Anna
Laptop
$1800

and:

Anna
Monitor
$420

A new combined results table appears in the centre of the frame with exactly FOUR columns:

name
product
total
customer_id

The table contains exactly TWO rows:

Anna | Laptop | $1800 | 101
Anna | Monitor | $420 | 101

MATCH ON customer_id = 101

<d>[English, Neutral Filipino Male Voice] SQL matches the shared ID and combines Anna with both of her orders.</d>

SELECT customers.name, orders.product, orders.total

customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id

A thick hand-drawn arrow points from:

101

in the CUSTOMERS table to:

101

in the ORDERS table.

Directly above the SQL query, large bold uppercase text appears:

JOIN = MATCH SHARED VALUES

<Subject 1> says:
<d>[English, Neutral Filipino Male Voice] The shared customer ID is the bridge that connects the two tables.</d>

At exactly 0:10, the combined results table shrinks rapidly into the presenter’s laptop screen, creating a clean transition into the next scene.
